approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph genetic optimizer whose evaluations are allocated by a Bayesian surrogate. It keeps the 64 best molecules it has actually had scored, draws breeding parents from the top score quantiles, and builds a surplus field of 160 fresh candidates per announced batch of ten: roughly two attempts in five recombine a connected fragment of two parents, the rest apply one to three successive single-atom or single-bond edits to one parent, with a longer walk only when the local neighbourhood keeps rejecting. Earlier children added the parts that now surround that generator: direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, every candidate must pass a stable canonical identity check and two duplicate scopes, and a narrow admission gate rejects any product that introduces a sulfur environment outside a fixed neutral envelope relative to its own scored parents. Which ten of the 160 candidates are evaluated is decided by a Gaussian process fitted only to this session's accepted scores, using integer-count Morgan fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto covariance; ten correlated draws from its joint posterior pick ten distinct candidates, and accepted scores feed straight back into the archive and the greedy population. Everything the optimizer can ever propose therefore comes from small graph edits of molecules it has already had scored.
approach.novelty: Give that surrogate a second kind of candidate to choose from: a quarter of the 160 pool slots are filled by a sequence model instead of a graph edit. During preparation, and only from the supplied unlabeled GuacaMol training corpus, the node trains a small autoregressive SMILES prior; during search that prior is frozen and objective-blind. For a prior-origin slot the same score-quantile parent draw selects a scored molecule, its canonical serialization is cut in half, and the prior writes a new ending for it in one pass, so a single proposal can rebuild a ring system and several atoms at once instead of moving one atom. The decoded product goes through exactly the inherited graph, identity, duplicate and sulfur checks, and the inherited correlated Thompson allocation still decides whether it is worth an evaluation. What distinguishes this from the siblings is the source of the chemistry: the three earlier proposal-source children on this Parent drew their larger moves from fixed tables and rules - local-context fragment substitution (-0.044214), BRICS-typed fragment crossover (-0.094793) and a fixed physicochemical niche breeding recipe (-0.055187) - and the whole round-39 to round-41 family changed only how many, how wide or how often, never what. This is the first child whose proposals come from a learned distribution over whole molecular strings. It is also not what the corpus-prior lineages elsewhere in the campaign do: they replaced the optimization loop with a policy-centred one, while this keeps L01's population, laws and validated allocator intact and lets the prior compete for a bounded share of the supply.

observed_bottleneck: On the sulfur-gated Anchor n-1744a1494180 the kind of molecule the search can propose, not the allocation of its evaluations, now bounds the endpoint. Its complete three-seed panel is 0.596453 (SD 0.033970) and all 27 complete children score lower (median -0.0478), while every law inside the K=3 stalled regime - amplitude, breadth, eligibility, regime duration, crossover presence, continuation presence, availability masking - lands inside the two gated law-free reference bands (n-47993ce5d053, n-843b25e73dee; best n-61b9b3bfb40d +0.010577), round 41 refuted the credit-driven walk-length law (n-0a7915ec6f8d -0.032994, falsifier triggered) and the ungated breeding-stream reference n-1c2f17550a3e measured -0.009888 for leaving the realization alone. The proposals themselves never change: the realized multi-call walk share is 0.180 and 2,550 of 2,860 accepted ordinary products come from a single mutation call, so the typical proposal is a one-atom edit of a founder-concentrated population. A read-only replay of the Anchor's own published seed-0 deco_hop and median_2 logs confirms it quantitatively: over its 580 accepted products the median radius-two 2048-bin count-Morgan Tanimoto to the best scored generating parent is 0.870, only 10.7 per cent sit at or below 0.70, the median heavy-atom change is one atom and only 15.7 per cent change three or more heavy atoms (0.0 per cent of mutation-only products, 41.7 per cent of crossover products). Curate records the same structural limitation from the other side (n-137ec411f54c, n-c7eb0cb7da3b, n-f84de4030e74, n-8b168a9969bb, n-189cd716f027): late search re-prices one scaffold through near score-identical single-atom swaps, and no allocation, duration or continuation child changes that chemistry. The campaign's own corpus-prior panels at this exact profile bound the opportunity and the risk: n-32ac3137615b holds deco_hop 0.814 and median_2 0.253671 against 0.706940 and 0.222732 here, n-dd7b8aa31113 holds median_2 0.238715, and both lose on sitagliptin_mpo (0.426, 0.376) where this Anchor holds 0.604768.

adoptions.applicability: The Anchor already supplies the paper's other required elements - a ranked scored population of 64, graph crossover and seven mutation operators, rank-like parent sampling - so only the missing element, the corpus-pretrained sequence policy as a proposal source, is added, and it is added where this Parent's measured limitation lies: the kind of chemistry proposed. It does not transfer to any claim about policy training, about GFlowNet credit, or about what the paper's full method would score here.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Maximum-likelihood pretraining of an autoregressive recurrent SMILES policy on an unlabeled corpus with no oracle calls, and per-round alternation in which policy-generated candidates and graph crossover/mutation offspring enter the same scored candidate set over a rank-selected population of 64, so one proposal can change several atoms and the ring system at once.

literature_review.conclusion: Adopt two elements and only two: unlabeled maximum-likelihood pretraining of an autoregressive SMILES prior on the supplied GuacaMol corpus (Genetic GFN's pretraining element, GuacaMol's corpus), and the alternation in which policy-generated and graph-generated candidates enter one scored candidate set over a rank-selected population of 64 (Genetic GFN). Adapt them to this profile: the prior supplies a preregistered quarter of the inherited 160-candidate pool instead of its own oracle batch, it is conditioned on a half-truncated serialization of the inherited score-quantile parent because a frozen prior is objective-blind, and it is a 2-layer GRU of the size this campaign's own prepare receipts support. Reject for this node the trajectory-balance update, the KL coefficient, the reward temperature, rank-weighted replay training, Augmented Memory-style score reuse, Saturn's architecture change, GuacaMol's hill-climbing fine-tuning, and every reported benchmark score of those papers, which are measured at 1,000 to 10,000 oracle calls under different metrics and are not campaign evidence. The conditions fit because the one element the Anchor lacks is exactly the element adopted, because the receipts show it is cheap enough to prepare inside the timeout, because the same Gaussian process has already allocated over a policy-generated pool in this campaign (n-cc2d839e347b), and because the three internal counterexamples on this Parent (n-9f11b684e560, n-55d120396e72, n-37a4fc183d94) say what must be measured first: whether a learned whole-sequence proposal is structurally farther than a table-cut graft, whether the allocator buys it, and whether it converts into realized incumbent increments rather than only into distinct chemistry.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The parent-prefix conditioning, the 0.25 share and the model size are settled by campaign receipts rather than by the sources: a frozen prior is objective-blind, so the inherited score-quantile parent draw is the only session signal this node is permitted to give it; the share must leave the inherited generator the majority of a fixed 160-candidate pool because that generator carries this Anchor's sitagliptin_mpo strength of 0.604768; and the model class is bounded by the campaign's own prepare receipt of 1,268,755 sequences to holdout token NLL 0.5685 in 240 s against a 3,600 s prepare timeout (n-dd7b8aa31113).

sources.applicability: This Anchor already has the scored population of 64, score-quantile (rank-like) parent sampling, two-parent connected-fragment crossover and seven mutation families; what it lacks is the corpus-pretrained sequence policy as a second candidate origin. Only the unlabeled maximum-likelihood prior and the per-round alternation of policy-generated with graph-generated candidates in one scored candidate set are adopted. The trajectory-balance update, KL coefficient, reward temperature and rank-weighted replay are not adopted in this node because the profile gives 300 accepted observations per task and the inherited Gaussian process, not the policy, decides what is evaluated.
sources.finding: Read the method and appendix: a recurrent GRU SMILES policy (embedding 128, hidden 512, three layers) is pretrained by maximum likelihood on ZINC 250K, reusing the PMO REINVENT prior and consuming no oracle information. Each round samples SMILES from the policy, scores them, and puts them in one buffer D together with Graph GA crossover and mutation offspring generated from a population initialized from D; the population size equals the batch size of 64 and was not tuned. The policy is then updated with a trajectory-balance loss (backward policy fixed to one for left-to-right generation) plus a KL penalty toward the pretrained prior, on replay batches sampled with weight proportional to (k|D| + rank(x))^-1 with k = 0.01 and reward inverse temperature 10, eight loops per round. Benchmarks use 10,000 oracle calls on PMO and 1,000 evaluations in the multi-objective study.

sources.finding: Defines the benchmark suite and its standardized training set derived from ChEMBL 24 by removing salts, neutralizing charges, dropping SMILES longer than 100 characters, restricting elements and removing molecules similar to a holdout of ten marketed drugs. Among goal-directed baselines the graph genetic algorithm scores highest in total (17.98) and the SMILES LSTM, a 3-layer network with hidden size 1024 trained on exactly that corpus and then hill-climbed for 20 rounds of 8,192 samples with top-1,024 fine-tuning, is second (17.34) while producing higher-quality molecules (about 77 per cent passing the quality filters against about 40 per cent for the graph GA).

method_change.previous_method: Proposals come only from graph edits of already scored molecules: two-parent connected-fragment crossover with optional finishing, or one to three successive single-atom/bond mutations under the floor-one law, with the Gaussian process and correlated Thompson allocation choosing ten of the resulting 160 candidates.
method_change.proposed_method: The same loop with a two-origin proposal supply: three quarters of the 160 pool slots keep the inherited graph-edit generator, and one quarter are whole-sequence continuations of a truncated serialization of the same score-quantile-sampled scored parent, sampled from a frozen corpus-pretrained autoregressive SMILES prior trained during preparation on the supplied unlabeled corpus. Allocation, admission, retention and every law stay inherited.
method_change.rationale: The state-conditioned axis of this Parent is measured out: every law inside its stalled regime sits inside the two gated law-free bands, the ungated reference n-1c2f17550a3e prices leaving the realization alone at -0.009888, and round 41 refuted the walk-length law (n-0a7915ec6f8d). Curate records that none of those children changes the kind of chemistry generated and that late search re-prices one scaffold through near score-identical single-atom edits; the Anchor's own logs give median Tanimoto 0.870 to the generating parent and zero multi-atom change among mutation-only products. The campaign has measured the alternative supply at this exact profile in other lineages (deco_hop 0.814 and median_2 0.253671 on n-32ac3137615b against 0.706940 and 0.222732 here) and has already allocated with this same Gaussian process over a policy-generated pool (n-cc2d839e347b), so a bounded prior-origin share is the smallest change that tests the generator rather than its schedule. It stays a component change: the method, its population, its laws and its selector are retained, and the prior only competes for a quarter of the supply.

hypothesis: Replace the generation path of a preregistered quarter of the Anchor's unchanged 160-candidate pool: for every admitted pool member whose index satisfies index mod 4 == 3 (40 of 160 slots), draw one scored parent with the inherited score-quantile law, tokenize that parent's canonical isomeric SMILES with the prior's Cl|Br|. token regex, keep the first ceil(T/2) content tokens as a fixed prefix, and sample a continuation from the frozen corpus-pretrained autoregressive SMILES prior at temperature 1.0 until the end-of-sequence token or the 192-token content cap; the decoded prefix-plus-continuation string is then offered to exactly the inherited admission path (checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission, both duplicate scopes, and the sulfur gate evaluated against that same single conditioning parent). At most twelve sampled continuations are spent on one prior-origin slot, after which that slot falls back to the inherited graph-edit path and the fallback is recorded. The prior is trained only during prepare, only on the supplied unlabeled corpus, and its weights are frozen for the whole session: no accepted score, no oracle label, no task identity and no gradient update ever reach it, and its only session-dependent input is the parent prefix. Every other Anchor component - the seven graph operator families and their probabilities, two-parent connected-fragment crossover and its optional finishing, the floor-one continuation law [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] with the rejection-conditioned escalation, score-quantile parent sampling, greedy-64 survival, the bounded refill and its attempt limits, the sulfur envelope and rejection bookkeeping, the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process with its generalized Tanimoto kernel, normalization, noise, jitter ladder and finite guards, and the correlated Thompson allocation with its availability masks and first-index ties - is retained exactly, and the pool target stays 160 so prior-origin candidates displace graph-edit slots rather than widening the field.

finding_summary.headline: The prior filled its quarter of every pool with far more distant chemistry; the surrogate bought 5.3% of picks, the panel fell 0.0519, median_2 rose 0.0114
finding_summary.insights:
The campaign has now changed what this Anchor can propose, and learned that proposal supply was not the binding constraint. The limitation has moved one stage downstream: the accepted-only count-fingerprint surrogate systematically prices unfamiliar chemistry below the incumbent's own neighbourhood, so a second, genuinely different generator can occupy a quarter of the supply and still receive one evaluation in twenty. That pricing is not a prior-origin artifact that fades; it hardens as the session proceeds, because each cheap prior evaluation that lands below the incumbent band teaches the same kernel to down-price its neighbours. This is the first measurement on this lineage that separates 'the generator cannot propose a scaffold jump' from 'the allocator will not pay for one', and it says the second is now the active obstacle.

The chemistry explains why the allocator was right in its own terms and still wrong for the campaign. The prior's products are farther and more makeable (median synthetic-accessibility score 2.4-4.1 against 3.0-5.2 for the edit path, almost no heteroatom-halogen bonds) but they land off the incumbent's scoring ridge: their median accepted score is 0.185 against 0.289, and not one of them appears in the highest-scoring thirty molecules of any of the fifteen sessions. A raw continuation keeps half of a scored parent's string and rewrites the rest, which is enough to leave the narrow composition window these objectives reward. The two origins were therefore not complementary at the level that matters here; one was chosen and the other was measured.

Two further limitations were measured rather than assumed. First, an unconditional prior prompted with a prefix degrades exactly where the population leaves corpus-like chemistry: sample parse rate ran 0.875 down to 0.232 across sessions, and the worst session (sitagliptin_mpo seed 2, 3,853 unparsable samples of 5,018, 88 slot fallbacks, 4.7 attempts per admitted member) is precisely the session that bought zero prior candidates. Prefix-conditioning an unconditional model is cheap but brittle off-distribution. Second, the inherited search behaviour that motivated this round is unchanged by a supply change alone: the molecular report still shows late search re-pricing one decorated framework (top-thirty sets spanning 3-16 Murcko scaffolds, up to 82% of a session's last hundred evaluations on one generic framework) and graph-edit products still at median Tanimoto 0.89 with a one-atom median change.

What this rules out and what it makes worth trying. It rules out 'the pool has the wrong chemistry in it' as the explanation for this Anchor's plateau, and with it the whole family of share, temperature, truncation and model-size variants of this recipe: exposure was already at the registered quarter and the structural prediction was met in full, so no parameter of this recipe is the missing piece. It points instead at method classes that change who gets evaluated or how a distant proposal is finished: an allocator that reserves evaluations by proposal family or prices novelty explicitly rather than one joint posterior over a mixed pool; a surrogate or ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes instead of a similarity kernel anchored on the archive; or a refinement stage that locally edits a continuation, or conditions on a longer prefix, so the prior's chemistry arrives already on the scoring ridge instead of competing raw against the incumbent's neighbourhood. Of the route's three reserved follow-ups, the retention and breeding-membership arm is the one that attacks the measured obstacle; unconditioned de novo sampling is contraindicated, because it would move proposals even farther from the archive, which is the direction this selector demonstrably refuses to buy; and a score-driven policy update would change the prior's distribution rather than the allocator's pricing, at a budget of 300 evaluations per task where the source method uses one to ten thousand.

Still open: the median_2 gain. It is the only task above the Anchor, it clears both its +0.010 bar and its reference band, and all three cells rose, but it cannot be attributed to the prior from this panel. Prior-origin products carry 0% of that session's increment mass on seed 0, 34.5% on seed 1 and 25.7% on seed 2, and the same intervention also cut the inherited graph field from 160 to about 120 candidates per batch, so the joint recipe, not the prior, is what moved. The complementary explanation Curate already recorded for median_2 - a compressed scoring band re-priced by near score-identical single-atom swaps - remains consistent with a 0.011 move. Also open is whether the panel loss is the prior's own cost or the ordinary price of leaving this Anchor's lucky realization: the panel sits 0.0011 below the ungated band edge, and its known deco_hop seed-0 departure cell alone is worth about -0.015.
finding_summary.results:
Supply changed exactly as registered. Across all fifteen sessions the frozen corpus prior filled 17,302 of the 69,600 admitted pool slots (realized share 0.2486 against the registered 0.25; every session at or above 0.231, every single pool at or above 0.194, 98 of 17,400 prior slots falling back to the graph path after the registered twelve attempts). The chemistry it supplied is much farther from its conditioning parent than the inherited graph edits of the same sessions: median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.609 against 0.833, 82.7% of prior members at or below 0.70 against 24.0%, median heavy-atom change four atoms against one, 70.3% changing at least three heavy atoms against 30.5%, and a changed Murcko core in 97.2% against 69.8%. The graph arm itself stayed inside the Anchor's own reference (accepted products: median 0.892 and 14.8% changing three or more atoms, against the Anchor's 0.889 and 13.1%). Preparation behaved: holdout token loss fell from about 4.56-4.59 to 0.563-0.566 on 1,268,755 corpus sequences per seed, with no oracle label, no stored molecule, and a parameter hash identical at the first and last batch of all fifteen sessions. None of the 231 accepted prior products is a verbatim corpus molecule.

The failure is at the point where the surrogate decides what to evaluate. The inherited correlated Thompson allocation spent 231 of 4,350 evaluations on prior-origin candidates, 5.3% of picks against a 24.9% share of the supply, and the registered range of 0.5 to 5 picks per batch of ten was missed in ten of fifteen sessions. 292 of 435 batches bought none at all, and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 bought none in any of its 29 batches, which is the registered allocation falsifier. The reason is visible in the posterior: in 433 of 435 batches both the median and the maximum predicted score of the prior-origin group sat below the graph-edit group, and that gap widened from 0.026 in the first ten batches to 0.115 and then 0.150 as each session's own accepted prior scores entered the archive; picks decayed accordingly, 140 then 55 then 36. The prior candidates that were bought were bought for their uncertainty, not their predicted value: median uncertainty percentile 0.78 and median predicted-score percentile 0.42 inside the pool, against 0.26 and 0.93 for graph-edit picks.

Conversion then failed on its own terms. Prior-origin products beat their own scored parent 25 times in 231 (0.108 against the graph arm's 0.148), produced 13 incumbent improvements against the graph arm's 241, and carried 0.1405 of the 5.0403 total realized incumbent-increment mass (2.8%). Eight of fifteen sessions saw no prior-origin incumbent improvement at all, against the registered requirement of at least one per session. Survival was weaker too: 67.5% of prior products entered the greedy-64 population against 79.6% of graph products, and prior-origin molecules were the conditioning parent in only 2.07% of the node's 111,107 parent draws. At node level the realized increment mass fell from the Anchor's 5.8194 to 5.0403 and incumbent improvements were 254 against 255, so the extra chemistry bought no extra realized gain.

Scores, complete and paired on seeds 0/1/2: panel mean 0.544512 against the Anchor's 0.596453, delta -0.051941, which sits just below the ungated law-free reference band's lower edge of -0.050871. Seed macros moved -0.096582, -0.049216 and -0.010026. Task means: deco_hop 0.617335 against 0.706940 (-0.089605, margin 0.02 breached, and this includes the known inherited seed-0 departure cell, 0.628292 here against 0.856148, worth about -0.0152 of the panel), sitagliptin_mpo 0.470835 against 0.604768 (-0.133933, margin breached), drd2_docking 0.955889 against 0.991017 (-0.035128, margin 0.03 breached), zaleplon_mpo 0.444399 against 0.456810 (-0.012411, inside its margin), median_2 0.234102 against 0.222732 (+0.011370, with all three cells above the Anchor's: +0.021327, +0.011740, +0.001043). The median_2 move is the only one that clears its registered band (upper edge +0.006695) and the only task mean above the Anchor. Interfaces were untouched: 160 candidates in all 435 pools, ten emitted in every batch, both duplicate scopes and a sulfur receipt on every valid novel candidate of both origins, 435 accepted-only model fits with no uncertainty escalation and no fallback batch, crossover share 0.432 against the Anchor's 0.429 and walk-length shares 0.817/0.152/0.030 against 0.814/0.155/0.031.

Supply changed exactly as registered. Across all fifteen sessions the frozen corpus prior filled 17,302 of the 69,600 admitted pool slots (realized share 0.2486 against the registered 0.25; every session at or above 0.231, every single pool at or above 0.194, 98 of 17,400 prior slots falling back to the graph path after the registered twelve attempts). The chemistry it supplied is much farther from its conditioning parent than the inherited graph edits of the same sessions: median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.609 against 0.833, 82.7% of prior members at or below 0.70 against 24.0%, median heavy-atom change four atoms against one, 70.3% changing at least three heavy atoms against 30.5%, and a changed Murcko core in 97.2% against 69.8%. The graph arm itself stayed inside the Anchor's own reference (accepted products: median 0.892 and 14.8% changing three or more atoms, against the Anchor's 0.889 and 13.1%). Preparation behaved: holdout token loss fell from about 4.56-4.59 to 0.563-0.566 on 1,268,755 corpus sequences per seed, with no oracle label, no stored molecule, and a parameter hash identical at the first and last batch of all fifteen sessions. None of the 231 accepted prior products is a verbatim corpus molecule.

The failure is at the point where the surrogate decides what to evaluate. The inherited correlated Thompson allocation spent 231 of 4,350 evaluations on prior-origin candidates, 5.3% of picks against a 24.9% share of the supply, and the registered range of 0.5 to 5 picks per batch of ten was missed in ten of fifteen sessions. 292 of 435 batches bought none at all, and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 bought none in any of its 29 batches, which is the registered allocation falsifier. The reason is visible in the posterior: in 433 of 435 batches both the median and the maximum predicted score of the prior-origin group sat below the graph-edit group, and that gap widened from 0.026 in the first ten batches to 0.115 and then 0.150 as each session's own accepted prior scores entered the archive; picks decayed accordingly, 140 then 55 then 36. The prior candidates that were bought were bought for their uncertainty, not their predicted value: median uncertainty percentile 0.78 and median predicted-score percentile 0.42 inside the pool, against 0.26 and 0.93 for graph-edit picks.

Conversion then failed on its own terms. Prior-origin products beat their own scored parent 25 times in 231 (0.108 against the graph arm's 0.148), produced 13 incumbent improvements against the graph arm's 241, and carried 0.1405 of the 5.0403 total realized incumbent-increment mass (2.8%). Eight of fifteen sessions saw no prior-origin incumbent improvement at all, against the registered requirement of at least one per session. Survival was weaker too: 67.5% of prior products entered the greedy-64 population against 79.6% of graph products, and prior-origin molecules were the conditioning parent in only 2.07% of the node's 111,107 parent draws. At node level the realized increment mass fell from the Anchor's 5.8194 to 5.0403 and incumbent improvements were 254 against 255, so the extra chemistry bought no extra realized gain.

Scores, complete and paired on seeds 0/1/2: panel mean 0.544512 against the Anchor's 0.596453, delta -0.051941, which sits just below the ungated law-free reference band's lower edge of -0.050871. Seed macros moved -0.096582, -0.049216 and -0.010026. Task means: deco_hop 0.617335 against 0.706940 (-0.089605, margin 0.02 breached, and this includes the known inherited seed-0 departure cell, 0.628292 here against 0.856148, worth about -0.0152 of the panel), sitagliptin_mpo 0.470835 against 0.604768 (-0.133933, margin breached), drd2_docking 0.955889 against 0.991017 (-0.035128, margin 0.03 breached), zaleplon_mpo 0.444399 against 0.456810 (-0.012411, inside its margin), median_2 0.234102 against 0.222732 (+0.011370, with all three cells above the Anchor's: +0.021327, +0.011740, +0.001043). The median_2 move is the only one that clears its registered band (upper edge +0.006695) and the only task mean above the Anchor. Interfaces were untouched: 160 candidates in all 435 pools, ten emitted in every batch, both duplicate scopes and a sulfur receipt on every valid novel candidate of both origins, 435 accepted-only model fits with no uncertainty escalation and no fallback batch, crossover share 0.432 against the Anchor's 0.429 and walk-length shares 0.817/0.152/0.030 against 0.814/0.155/0.031.

The campaign has now changed what this Anchor can propose, and learned that proposal supply was not the binding constraint. The limitation has moved one stage downstream: the accepted-only count-fingerprint surrogate systematically prices unfamiliar chemistry below the incumbent's own neighbourhood, so a second, genuinely different generator can occupy a quarter of the supply and still receive one evaluation in twenty. That pricing is not a prior-origin artifact that fades; it hardens as the session proceeds, because each cheap prior evaluation that lands below the incumbent band teaches the same kernel to down-price its neighbours. This is the first measurement on this lineage that separates 'the generator cannot propose a scaffold jump' from 'the allocator will not pay for one', and it says the second is now the active obstacle.

The chemistry explains why the allocator was right in its own terms and still wrong for the campaign. The prior's products are farther and more makeable (median synthetic-accessibility score 2.4-4.1 against 3.0-5.2 for the edit path, almost no heteroatom-halogen bonds) but they land off the incumbent's scoring ridge: their median accepted score is 0.185 against 0.289, and not one of them appears in the highest-scoring thirty molecules of any of the fifteen sessions. A raw continuation keeps half of a scored parent's string and rewrites the rest, which is enough to leave the narrow composition window these objectives reward. The two origins were therefore not complementary at the level that matters here; one was chosen and the other was measured.

Two further limitations were measured rather than assumed. First, an unconditional prior prompted with a prefix degrades exactly where the population leaves corpus-like chemistry: sample parse rate ran 0.875 down to 0.232 across sessions, and the worst session (sitagliptin_mpo seed 2, 3,853 unparsable samples of 5,018, 88 slot fallbacks, 4.7 attempts per admitted member) is precisely the session that bought zero prior candidates. Prefix-conditioning an unconditional model is cheap but brittle off-distribution. Second, the inherited search behaviour that motivated this round is unchanged by a supply change alone: the molecular report still shows late search re-pricing one decorated framework (top-thirty sets spanning 3-16 Murcko scaffolds, up to 82% of a session's last hundred evaluations on one generic framework) and graph-edit products still at median Tanimoto 0.89 with a one-atom median change.

What this rules out and what it makes worth trying. It rules out 'the pool has the wrong chemistry in it' as the explanation for this Anchor's plateau, and with it the whole family of share, temperature, truncation and model-size variants of this recipe: exposure was already at the registered quarter and the structural prediction was met in full, so no parameter of this recipe is the missing piece. It points instead at method classes that change who gets evaluated or how a distant proposal is finished: an allocator that reserves evaluations by proposal family or prices novelty explicitly rather than one joint posterior over a mixed pool; a surrogate or ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes instead of a similarity kernel anchored on the archive; or a refinement stage that locally edits a continuation, or conditions on a longer prefix, so the prior's chemistry arrives already on the scoring ridge instead of competing raw against the incumbent's neighbourhood. Of the route's three reserved follow-ups, the retention and breeding-membership arm is the one that attacks the measured obstacle; unconditioned de novo sampling is contraindicated, because it would move proposals even farther from the archive, which is the direction this selector demonstrably refuses to buy; and a score-driven policy update would change the prior's distribution rather than the allocator's pricing, at a budget of 300 evaluations per task where the source method uses one to ten thousand.

Still open: the median_2 gain. It is the only task above the Anchor, it clears both its +0.010 bar and its reference band, and all three cells rose, but it cannot be attributed to the prior from this panel. Prior-origin products carry 0% of that session's increment mass on seed 0, 34.5% on seed 1 and 25.7% on seed 2, and the same intervention also cut the inherited graph field from 160 to about 120 candidates per batch, so the joint recipe, not the prior, is what moved. The complementary explanation Curate already recorded for median_2 - a compressed scoring band re-priced by near score-identical single-atom swaps - remains consistent with a 0.011 move. Also open is whether the panel loss is the prior's own cost or the ordinary price of leaving this Anchor's lucky realization: the panel sits 0.0011 below the ungated band edge, and its known deco_hop seed-0 departure cell alone is worth about -0.015.

molecular.headline: Small fused heteroaromatics, flat and achiral, climbing by terminal-atom swaps onto ring nitrogen; the prior's farther molecules stay below the incumbent band.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five proposal sets this node emitted 870 molecules per objective (4,350 total, 4,374 unique strings) that are mid-sized, ring-dense and essentially flat: median 23-36 heavy atoms, 3-5 rings of which 2-4 aromatic, digest ring_closure_rate 0.959-0.987 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.834-0.981, fused-ring membership in 21-97 per cent of molecules, fraction sp3 carbon 0.21-0.35. Not one molecule in any of the 15 sessions carries a stereo bond marker: the digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five sets and the '@' character does not occur in any of the 15 trajectory files, even though the median molecule on two sets has two undefined sp3 stereocentres. Charge is absent (charged_rate 0.0-0.0034). The chemistry the score rewards is reached almost entirely by changing a terminal heteroatom or halogen rather than the carbon framework: ring-nitrogen substituted with F, Cl, OH, SH or OCH2Cl (65/870 heteroatom-halogen bonds on one set), halomethyl ethers, acyl fluorides (204/870 on one set), free thiols (164/870 on another), vinyl halides and strained aziridine substituents (31/870). Functional-group range is otherwise thin: oxidised sulfur is near absent where the founders lack it (sulfone 1-5/870, sulfonamide 0-2/870 on four of the five sets), and the 231 molecules that came from the new corpus prior are the most makeable and the farthest from their parent (median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.62-0.69, median heavy-atom change 2-6, median SA score 2.4-4.1) yet sit in a lower score band and none of them appears in the highest-scoring 30 of any session.

per_task.generated_character: Compact tricyclic heteroaromatics, median 24 heavy atoms, 3 rings all aromatic, QED median 0.71, SA score median 3.0, no stereochemistry and no charge. Two families dominate: a methoxy/ethyl-decorated indole or azaindole bearing a 4-cyanophenyl or cyanopyridyl ring (CCc1cc2[nH]c(-c3ccc(C#N)nc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC, 0.4584), and a pyrazolo-fused lactam N-aryl series (CCOc1cc2cc3n(c2nc1C)N(c1cccc(C)c1)C3=O, 0.4584). 94 per cent of the set has a fused ring system (digest ring_closure_rate 0.9713, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9701).
liabilities: N-hydroxy, N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-thio pyrrole nitrogens drive the top of the ranking (n2O, n2F, n2S, n2Cl)
chloromethyl and fluoromethyl ethers appear in 16 per cent of the top-30 (OCCl, OCF)
65 of 870 molecules carry a heteroatom-halogen bond and 69 an N-O or N-S single bond
degenerate micro-molecules consume budget: OBr, ClCl, OOCl, FCl, NCl, C1COC1 all scored 0.0
missing_features: no acetamide or N,N-dialkylamide side chain of the kind the initial 0.3051 hit carried into the run
no saturated N-heterocycle anywhere in the 90 highest-scoring molecules (ring basic amine 0 per cent of top-30)
no sulfone or sulfonamide in the top-30 and only 2 sulfones in 870 proposals
no defined stereochemistry at all (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0)
no polar neutral groups beyond methoxy and nitrile; carboxylic acid 0 per cent, urea 0 per cent, ester 0 per cent
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with the aryl nitrile plus dimethoxy/ethyl decoration pattern and, bluntly, with whatever substituent sits on the pyrrole nitrogen: the three best molecules differ from mid-field siblings only in that heteroatom. CCc1cc2c(cc(-c3ccc(C#N)cn3)n2O)c(OC)c1C scores 0.4720 with N-OH, the N-F analogue CCc1cc2c(cc(-c3ccc(C#N)nc3)n2F)c(OC)c1OC 0.4531, while the N-ethyl analogue CCc1cc2c(cc(-c3ccc(C#N)cn3)n2CC)c(OC)c1OC collapses to 0.1527. The gradient is a composition/size window, not a pharmacophore: 37 of 870 proposals score exactly zero and all of them are fragments or mis-sized molecules.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the run: median 36 heavy atoms, 4 rings, 4 aromatic, mean SMILES length 63.6 and max 133, QED median 0.30, SA score median 3.92, halogen in 67 per cent of strings. Two shapes recur: a fluorinated biaryl hinged onto a pyrimidine-fused spiro/oxazine core and decorated with nitrile and haloalkene arms (CC1(C)COc2nc1nc1ncnc(-c3cccc(-c4cnc(C=C(F)Cl)c(C#N)c4C(Cl)=CF)c3F)c21, 0.6261), and in the third seed a poly-triazole chain of N-methyl-1,2,3-triazoles linked N-N and through an aryl ether (CC(=O)c1cccc(Oc2nn(C)n2Nc2nn(C)n2-c2nc(C)ccc2C)n1, 0.6127).
liabilities: haloalkene and 1-halo-1-propenyl arms on heteroarenes (C(Cl)=CF, C=C(F)Cl) in a third of the top-30
chloromethyl/fluoromethyl ethers in 29 per cent of the top-30 (OCCl, CF in OCC5(C)CF)
N-N linked triazole chains and an O-triazolyl ether in the seed-2 endgame are strained, hydrolytically fragile motifs
acyclic amidine and imino ether fragments appear in late molecules (C(=N)Oc1nn(C)n1, N=C(F)Cl)
26 of 870 proposals have 6 or fewer heavy atoms yet still return 0.5000
missing_features: no sulfone or sulfonamide in any of the 90 highest-scoring molecules and only 2 sulfones in 870 proposals
no sulfur at all in the top-90, although 125 of 870 proposals contain sulfur somewhere
no aminoheteroaryl (NH-linked bicyclic) hinge; amide drops to 8 per cent in the top-30
no saturated amine ring (ring basic amine 0 per cent of top-30)
no defined stereochemistry and no charged group
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks size, lipophilicity and halogen count more than any recognisable functional group: the 90 highest-scoring molecules have median 38 heavy atoms, logP 5.26 and 4 halogens with vinyl halide in 33 per cent and halomethyl ether in 29 per cent, against 32 heavy atoms, logP 2.55 and 1 halogen in the lowest 100. Amide content falls from 19 per cent at the bottom to 8 per cent at the top, so the gradient is pulling polarity out. The whole set is compressed into a narrow band (digest span 0.2827-0.6283, median 0.5887) and even trivial fragments such as C#C and ClCCl score 0.5000, so the objective gives most of its credit before any chemistry is proposed.

per_task.generated_character: The least ring-fused and most lipophilic set: median 34 heavy atoms, 3 rings but only 2 aromatic, fused systems in just 21 per cent, fraction sp3 0.35, logP median 5.75, halogen in 99 per cent of strings, two undefined sp3 stereocentres in the median molecule. The recurring shape is a diarylmethane or 1,1-diaryl cyclopentane carrying an acyclic N-methyl-N-propylamine and a chlorinated or brominated ring: CCCN(C)C(c1cccc(S)c1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1CCN (0.9999) and CCCc1cc(Cl)ccc1C1(CN(C)CCC)c2cc(Cl)cc(c2)C1Cl (0.9999).
liabilities: free aryl and alkyl thiols in 46 per cent of the top-30 (c1cccc(S)c1, SCO, SO), which are oxidation-prone and odorous
primary alkyl amine tails (CCN) in 177 of 870 proposals used as an extra basic centre
sulfinamide and sulfoxide fragments (NS(=O)c1...) in 245 of 870 proposals
chloro-cyclopentane and gem-dihalo sp3 carbons in the top scorers (C1Cl in C1(CN(C)CCC)c2cc(Cl)cc(c2)C1Cl)
logP above 5 in the median molecule; QED median 0.25
missing_features: the basic nitrogen is almost never in a ring: saturated ring amine in 7 per cent of the top-30 here, against 96 per cent in the Parent's own top-30 on the same objective
no piperazine in any high scorer; the amine is an acyclic N(C)CCC chain
no defined configuration on the benzylic stereocentre that every top molecule carries
no aromatic-ring nitrogen in the lipophilic ring (aromatic rings are plain benzenes)
no amide or carbamate linker retained at the top; the molecules are held together by C-C bonds only
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The one feature that separates top from bottom is a basic amine: 100 per cent of the 90 highest-scoring molecules carry one against 43 per cent of the lowest 100, while amide (66 to 1 per cent), carboxylic acid (52 to 29 per cent) and sulfonamide (39 to 0 per cent) are all penalised, and TPSA drops from 103 to 71. The initial sulfonyl-bearing molecules score 0.0002-0.0016 (COC1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1) and the search climbs by stripping the sulfonamide, adding an aryl chloride and hanging a tertiary amine on a benzylic carbon.

per_task.generated_character: The most ring-dense and most drug-like set: median 31 heavy atoms, 5 rings, 3 aromatic, 97 per cent fused, QED median 0.59, SA score median 3.49, halogen in only 11 per cent of strings, no stereochemistry. The molecules read as literal hybrids of two reference chemotypes: a propyl-ethoxyphenyl ring joined to a benzimidazole-bearing pyrazolo-tetrahydropyridine with an N-methyl amine (CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-n2nc3c(c2-c2nc4ccccc4[nH]2)CCN(C)CC3)c1, 0.2331), and a methylenedioxyphenyl-substituted pyrazolo-fused diketopiperazine (CCC1C(=O)c2c(nn(Cc3ccc4c(c3)OCO4)c2N2CC2)CN(C)C1=O, 0.2334).
liabilities: aziridine substituents on the pyrazole (N2CC2) in 21 per cent of the top-30 and 31 of 870 proposals; this is a strained, alkylating motif that the score rewards
aminal and N-N-C-N arrangements in 19 per cent of the set (N2Cn3c4c2[nH]..., C2=C(N3CC3)NN(...)N=C2)
N-O and N-S single bonds in 79 of 870 proposals
late molecules fuse four rings into bridged cages of questionable stability (CCOc1ccc(CC)cc1N1C2Cc3ccccc3CN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(N2)C31)
missing_features: no sulfonamide or sulfonyl-piperazine anywhere near the top: sulfonamide 2 of 870 and 0 of the top-90
no defined stereochemistry on any of the fused saturated rings
no piperazine ring; the basic nitrogen is an N-methyl in a fused 6-ring or an acyclic methylamine
no carboxamide-to-aryl linker chemistry beyond the lactam already inherited
almost no halogen or trifluoromethyl decoration (halogen in 11 per cent of strings)
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rewards carrying both reference motifs at once on a fused core: amide rises from 26 per cent in the lowest 100 to 67 per cent in the top-30, ring basic amine from 28 to 59 per cent, N-N linkage from 2 to 13 per cent and fused-ring membership to 100 per cent, while plain ester falls from 58 to 0 per cent and aromatic ring count drops from 3 to 2. The whole band is compressed (digest best 0.2358, median 0.1926), so single-atom swaps on one hybrid re-price by thousandths and 5 proposals score exactly zero (C, C#C, OF).

per_task.generated_character: Heavily fluorinated, densely fused and the least makeable set of the run: median 27 heavy atoms, 5 rings but only 2 aromatic, 94 per cent fused, SA score median 5.15 (top-30 median 5.49), halogen in 88 per cent of strings, digest aromatic_atom_rate the lowest at 0.8345. The high scorers are bridged tetracyclic lactams carrying a 2-hydroxy-cyclopentadienyl ring and fluoromethyl/fluorovinyl arms: O=C1NC2C(CF)N(O)c3cn(C4=CC(F)C=C4O)c(c31)CN2C=CF (0.5467) and N=c1c2c3n(C4=CC(F)C=C4O)cc2n(CCF)c(=O)n1Cn1ccc(F)c1-3 (0.4967).
liabilities: acyl fluorides in 204 of 870 proposals, including the seed-1 top molecules (C(=O)F on a cyclohexadiene)
N-hydroxy amine in a fused ring (N(O)) and N-F/N-S bonds in 63 of 870 proposals
enamine-type N-vinyl fluoride arms (N2C=CF) in 40 per cent of the top-30
non-aromatic cyclopentadienol and cyclohexadienone rings used as the aryl surrogate (C4=CC(F)C=C4O)
SA score median 5.15 rising to 5.49 in the top-30: the gradient is pushing toward less makeable molecules
36 of 870 proposals have 6 or fewer heavy atoms (F, Cl, C#C, FCF) and score zero
missing_features: no defined stereochemistry, although the top molecules each carry two undefined sp3 stereocentres
no primary or secondary beta-amino amide; basic amine appears in 0 per cent of the top-30 and 2 per cent of the set
no trifluoromethyl group (CF3 in 1 per cent of the set) and no trifluorophenyl ring
no aromatic triazole or triazolopyrazine; the nitrogen-rich rings generated are saturated or non-aromatic
no benzene ring retained in the top scorers: aromatic ring count drops to 1 in the top-30, the fluorinated ring is a cyclopentadiene
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score follows fluorine count and ring fusion, not any recognisable amine pharmacophore: the top-30 median has 3 halogens and 100 per cent fused rings with vinyl fluoride in 40 per cent, against 1 halogen and 84 per cent fused in the lowest 100. The objective is close to all-or-nothing on this generator: digest median 0.1162 with a worst of ~7.7e-27 and 69 of 870 proposals at zero, including bare F, Cl and C#C, and the session ends on FCF at 0.0000 after a 0.4535-class molecule, so a single bad edit falls the whole way out of the scoring region.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The '@' character does not occur once in the 15 trajectory files (4,500 lines), the digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five proposal sets, and yet the median molecule on two of the sets carries two undefined sp3 stereocentres and the highest-scoring molecules are built around saturated bridged rings whose configuration is left unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits defined stereochemistry, on any molecule, in any session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: No operator in the current family can set, flip or inherit a chiral tag, and the serialization path drops configuration. A task-agnostic generator needs a stereochemistry-aware proposal operator (assign or invert a tetrahedral centre, set double-bond geometry) and a canonicalization that preserves it, so that any objective sensitive to configuration can be reached at all rather than approached by achiral surrogates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Oxidised sulfur is effectively unreachable: 1-5 sulfones and 0-2 sulfonamides per 870 proposals on four of the five sets. Where the initial population did carry an arylsulfonamide, the search deleted it instead: sulfonamide falls from 39 per cent of the lowest-scoring 100 to 0 per cent of the highest-scoring 90, and no sulfone or sulfonamide survives into any top-30 of the whole run. The same holds for carboxamide-to-heteroaryl hinges and for saturated amine rings, which appear in 7 per cent of one set's top-30 against 96 per cent of the comparison baseline's top-30 on the same objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: Multi-atom functional groups cannot be installed de novo; the generator only re-prices what the founders already carried.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom replace/append/delete operators cannot assemble a three- or four-atom group in one accepted step, so any group absent from the population stays absent for the whole budget. The generator needs fragment-level attachment from a fixed chemically-sensible group library (sulfonyl, sulfonamide, amide, saturated azacycle, trifluoromethyl) as a first-class operator, independent of what the founders happened to contain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring nitrogens substituted with OH, F, Cl, SH or OCH2Cl carry the top of one set (0.4720 for the N-OH form, 0.4531 for N-F, 0.1527 for the ordinary N-ethyl analogue). Across the run there are 65, 68, 61, 13 and 63 heteroatom-halogen bonds per 870 proposals, 204 acyl fluorides on one set, 164 free thiols on another, 31 aziridine substituents that appear in 21 per cent of one top-30, plus halomethyl ethers in up to 29 per cent of a top-30 and vinyl halides in up to 40 per cent.
transferable_gaps.gap: The cheapest way to move the score is a terminal heteroatom or halogen swap, so the search climbs through bonds that are not chemically viable.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator probabilities make a one-atom substituent change on a heteroatom the dominant accepted move, and no stability or valence-context filter rejects heteroatom-halogen, N-O, N-S, acyl halide, free thiol or strained three-membered-ring motifs. A generator should price such edits out, either with a chemical-stability admission filter or by making carbon-skeleton edits of comparable cost, so that score gain has to come from the framework rather than from a labile terminal atom.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each proposal set contains 10-36 molecules of 6 or fewer heavy atoms, and the digest's worst lists are almost entirely such fragments: OBr, ClCl, OOCl, FCl, NCl, C1COC1, C, OF, C#C, CCl, FCF, bare F and bare Cl. On two sets these are exact zeros (37 and 69 proposals at zero score respectively), and one session's very last evaluation was spent on FCF.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nothing stops degenerate micro-molecules from consuming oracle evaluations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The admission path accepts any parsable string, so deletion-heavy edit chains can walk a parent down to a two-atom fragment and still spend a scored evaluation on it. A heavy-atom floor, or an admission rule tied to the conditioning parent's size, would convert those evaluations into usable proposals on every objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-seed highest-scoring 30 molecules span only 3-16 distinct Murcko scaffolds and 1-11 generic frameworks (one session's top-30 is a single generic framework), the last 100 evaluations of a session are up to 82 per cent the same generic framework as the best molecule, and graph-edit products sit at median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.87-0.92 to their conditioning parent with a median heavy-atom change of exactly 1.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search collapses onto one decorated framework and re-prices it one atom at a time.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Parent selection plus single-atom edits turns the back half of every budget into a local re-pricing of one framework. A generator needs a scaffold-level jump that is admitted on its own terms - diversity-aware pool admission, or an operator that replaces a whole ring system - rather than a higher mutation count on the same core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 231 of the 4,350 accepted products came from the prior. They are structurally farther from their conditioning parent (median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.62-0.69 against 0.87-0.92 for the edit path, median heavy-atom change 2-6 against 1), more makeable (median SA score 2.38-4.09 against 3.01-5.16) and cleaner (for instance 0-1 per cent carry a heteroatom-halogen bond). Their score medians are nevertheless 0.00-0.19 against 0.13-0.54 for the edit path on the same sets, and none of them appears in the highest-scoring 30 of any of the 15 sessions.
transferable_gaps.gap: The prefix-conditioned sequence prior supplies farther and more makeable molecules but enters below the incumbent score band, and nothing then refines them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A corpus-trained continuation of a parent prefix reaches chemistry the edit operators cannot, but it lands off the incumbent's scoring ridge and is then evaluated as-is. A generator that wants both would have to refine such proposals before they are scored - local edits seeded on the continuation, or continuation from a longer prefix so the parent's scoring motif is retained - rather than offer them raw and in competition with the incumbent's own neighbourhood.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest charged_rate is 0.0000-0.0034 on the five sets, and the only charged species seen anywhere in the trajectories is a single nitro group. No protonated amine, carboxylate, amidinium or quaternary nitrogen is ever proposed, even on the set where a basic amine is present in 100 per cent of the highest-scoring 90 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Charged and zwitterionic chemistry is absent from the whole output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set only ever produces neutral valence-complete atoms, so any objective whose chemistry is expressed at a charged centre is approached only through its neutral surrogate. A generator should be able to propose formally charged or zwitterionic forms and have the admission path accept them.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
